pole_argument: At a=3,v=2 the saved monic discriminant is squarefree. Since its generic leading coefficient is 27a^2, this proves generic squarefreeness.
Away from Delta all coefficients and T are regular, so a rational K cannot have a finite pole.
At a simple Delta root, residue eigenvalues are 0 and -1/3. T has order at most two; K can therefore have at most a simple pole.
G=diag(t^-3,t^-1); Nbar=O(t^-2) and G*T=O(t^-2). A positive-degree polynomial part of G*K is impossible. Hence K0=O(t^3), K1=O(t), giving deg(P0)<=15,deg(P1)<=13 for K=P/monic(Delta).

The generic coefficient system and rhs are regular at a=3,v=2. Full column rank30 there supplies an invertible30x30 minor; by Cramer a putative generic solution would be regular there, contradicting exact rank30 versus31. Thus no rational K in Q(a,v,t)^2 solves this displayed universal-family equation.
